fatal_errors: The proposed severe-plastic-deformation/annealing intervention does not reconstruct the target intervention of varying Mo content in a Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3-containing CoCrFeNiMox composite.

The cited evidence concerns a chemically distinct Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 alloy whose high-temperature glaze relies partly on alumina nanoparticles and composition undulation; it does not establish that annealed CoCrFeNi will form stable Cr-rich nanoprecipitates or an equivalent protective glaze.

The claim that high grain-boundary density directly reduces low-temperature friction through plastic accommodation is not adequately supported and may conflict with the increased deformation and adhesion that can occur in nanostructured metals.
explanation: The hypothesis directly addresses wide-temperature sliding of CoCrFeNi and offers a testable processing-based alternative, but it has little agreement with the hidden target. It omits Mo-induced lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening, the Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 lubricant package, and the low-temperature sulfide/silver films and high-temperature silver-molybdate glaze central to the target. Its conditions only partially agree: air, 25–800 °C, and a load range containing 8 N are specified, but counterface, speed, sliding distance, and discrete test temperatures are absent, while a continuous ramp would confound temperature with accumulated wear. The predicted improvement is qualitative and uses an unspecified coarse-grained alloy rather than the Mo0.2 composite baseline. The controlled comparison, friction and wear measurements, microscopy, and explicit falsification threshold make the experiment reasonably discriminating, although fixed temperatures, identical 8 N conditions, replication, counterface specification, and post-test phase/oxide analysis would be needed. The external evidence supports the general adaptive-interface concept but not the proposed route or chemistry in CoCrFeNi, so the hypothesis remains a weakly supported plausible alternative rather than a reconstruction.
